pitfalls: No LiteRT-LM release ran this file on the card's date: from PyPI, LiteRT-LM 0.19.0 stops on the CPU with `moe node #85 unsupported activation='silu'` and on the GPU with `moe only supports activation='gelu_tanh' (or its legacy spelling 'gelu')`. SiLU in the moe op is in the LiteRT pull requests #11192 (GPU kernel) and #11188 (XNNPACK kernel, CPU), open on 2026-11-03; the card's numbers come from a LiteRT-LM built from source with both (card L23, L76-L96).

On a LiteRT-LM built from source with #11192 and #11188 (not a release), the card measured this file on an Apple M4 Max (128 GB, macOS 27.0), 1,024 prefill and 256 decode tokens, 2026-11-03: WebGPU prefill 778.11 tok/s, decode 47.64 tok/s, peak physical footprint 34.14 GB; CPU (XNNPACK) 56.30 / 4.16 tok/s, 5.37 GB; on its 12 check questions and a 3-turn conversation, the same verdict as Transformers 12 / 12, the stop token 12 / 12, 3 turns pass on both backends (card L19, L47-L53, L62-L68).
Keep the fp32 activation declaration: with fp16 activations every one of the 8 check questions run repeated a short passage of its thought until the token limit, without an answer (card L41).
Every GPU check on the card ran with --sampler_handles_input=false; the default GPU sampler path was compared on one 64-token reply only (card L70).
Thinking is on by default: the CLI prints the thought between [thought] and [/thought], then the answer; the sampler is TOP_P (top_p 0.95, top_k 20, temperature 0.6) (card L21, L40, L108).
Int4 attention and lm_head weights were not faster than int8 ones on WebGPU (41.9 against 41.1 tokens/s) and one of the 12 check questions looped with them, so the files keep them int8 (card L42).
Size: 20.65 GB; no phone was tried (card L30, L58).
